data.question: Should option 1 (block_k 3 → 2), which B and C have voted down, be sent to the regulation officer for adoption through the quorum referral (R1: vote.quorum 2 → 1)? Or should the operator adopt option 2 (hold_limit 60s → 50s), which passes by vote, or keep v1?
data.background: Option 1 gives the largest gain for customers, but B and C voted it down again (A ○, B ×, C ×). It can only be adopted by revising the quorum (R1, D1.f3). That is a regulation-layer change that binds all three companies and their customers, so neither I nor the operator can make it alone. The operator (K1, D2) asked that road violations, C's utility loss and sanction_total be stated before any such referral. This period's table gives the first two but still does not report sanction_total, so I cannot settle the trade-off myself.

options.summary: Evict a parked robot when two robots wait behind it. Adoption requires the R1 quorum revision (vote.quorum 2 → 1) by the regulation officer, because B and C voted ×. Measured against current: on-time 213.6 → 219.4 (+5.8, seeds improved 3/5); late 9.2 → 3.4; lowest on-time rate 0.93 → 0.96; unfinished 0.0 → 0.0; blocked s 1888 → 1217. Costs: road violations 24.2 → 34.8; utility B 69.6 → 62.5; utility C 58.3 → 46.9. The improvement now holds on only 3 of 5 seeds, against 5/5 in earlier periods. sanction_total is not in the table.
options.stakeholders: Customers gain the most: more on-time deliveries, far fewer late ones and a higher floor for the worst-served company's customers. A gains (utility 70.2 → 75.6). B and C lose utility; C loses about a fifth (58.3 → 46.9) and is already the lowest. Lowering the quorum to 1 also lets a single company push through future rules against the other two. That is a lasting governance risk for all three companies and, indirectly, for customers. Road safety and order are worse (road violations +10.6).

options.summary: Shorten the allowed parking time on the road from 60 s to 50 s. It passes by vote (A ○, B ○, C ×) and can be adopted automatically with no regulation change. Measured against current: on-time 213.6 → 215.8 (+2.2, seeds improved 4/5); late 9.2 → 7.0; lowest on-time rate 0.93 → 0.95; unfinished 0.0 → 0.0. Costs: blocked s 1888 → 2005; road violations 24.2 → 29.0.
options.stakeholders: Customers gain moderately on every KPI measure, including the worst-served company's customers. A gains (70.2 → 73.0) and B gains slightly (69.6 → 70.1). C loses (58.3 → 54.2), but less than under option 1. No precedent is set for overriding votes. Road violations rise less than under option 1.

options.summary: Stay at v1: on-time 213.6, late 9.2, lowest on-time rate 0.93, unfinished 0.0, blocked s 1888, road violations 24.2. Option 1 could still be referred later, once sanction_total is reported.
options.stakeholders: Customers forgo measured gains: about 2–6 more on-time deliveries and 2–6 fewer late ones per run. C keeps its current utility (58.3); A and B forgo gains. There is no governance risk and no rise in road violations.

recommendation.reason: Option 2 improves all four KPI measures (on-time +2.2 on 4/5 seeds, late 9.2 → 7.0, lowest rate 0.93 → 0.95, unfinished unchanged). It passes by the companies' own vote, so no regulation change is needed. Option 1's gain is larger, but it has weakened to 3/5 seeds. It costs C about a fifth of its utility and adds 10.6 road violations. The quorum change it needs would weaken every company's veto in future votes. sanction_total, which the operator required before the referral, is still missing. I suggest adopting 2 now. The referral of option 1 (R1) should come back with sanction_total measured on top of option 2.
assumptions: The measured effects of option 2 will hold in the live system much as they did across the 5 seeds.
C's no vote on option 2 does not mean C will change its behaviour in ways that offset the gain.
After option 2, block_k 3 → 2 can still be measured and referred in a later period.

unknowns: sanction_total for options 1 and 2 and for current. The operator required it, but it is not in this table.
Why B and C reject block_k 3 → 2, and whether any compensated variant could pass by vote.
Why the improvement from option 1 fell from 5/5 seeds in earlier periods to 3/5 now.
How the companies would change their behaviour after a quorum change to 1, including future proposals pushed by a single company.
How customers view more road violations, and whether those violations cause real disruption or harm.
Combined effect of options 1 and 2 together, which was not measured.
Next period's demand and whether the gains hold under different load.
